chapter: Image, travel and Black, Brown and Beige
title: The Carnegie Hall premiere in a blizzard
summary: The hall was packed despite the blizzard and Ellington returned every year with a new program.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: And then after that you all presented it in New York?
Yeah, we laid it on Carnegie Hall. We laid it smack, dab on them, man, killed them.
Now, wasn't it a terrible snowstorm that you all performed in?
That was the biggest blizzard New York had. Because my wife and my daughter was down. Couldn't no

cabs run. We were living up in the Bronx then. The only way we got home, a friend of mine who had one of them Army trucks, charged $1.00 a head, they were getting rough! That's the way we got home. It was a blizzard, man. It was one of them hard, hard, hard blizzards. I think a lot of people, they just kept the hall open all night long because the people couldn't get home.
Did many people turn out, anyway?
Oh, the whole hall, it was packed.
Oh, even with the blizzard it was packed?

Didn't mean a thing. Packed and jammed, hanging on the ceiling, chandeliers, you know. We was packed. Because when the concert -- the blizzard didn't start until after the concert started. Nobody thought -- like that was one of the big blizzards in New York. That's right. We laid that on them. We laid that on Carnegie Hall. And every year after that, the man say, you ought to come back, every year we'd come back. Come back with a different program. We would play -- Benny Goodman played, well, anytime he can play, he's going to play the same tunes. But everytime -- that's why the man liked it. We had a complete program, new. It wasn't something people heard before, and they knew that. They looked for that. Never disappointed.
